questions.question: In February 2025, the Union Budget 2025–26 announced the establishment of which board in Bihar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Makhana Board**__.

• During the presentation of the **Union Budget 2025–26** on **February 1, 2025**, Union Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** announced the establishment of a **Makhana Board** in the state of **Bihar**.
 
• The primary objective of the **Makhana Board** is to provide a structured institutional framework for the **research**, **production**, **processing**, and **international branding** of **Makhana** (also known as **foxnuts** or **Gorgon nuts**).
 
• **Bihar** is the undisputed leader in **Makhana** production, contributing more than **85% to 90%** of the total global supply, making it a vital component of the state's **agrarian economy**.
 
• The board is expected to help farmers adopt **modern technology** for harvesting and processing, which is currently labor-intensive and largely traditional.

questions.question: How many sports were featured in the Khelo India Youth Games, 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**28**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG) 2025** marked the **8th edition** of this prestigious national-level multi-sport competition.
 
• For the **2025** edition, the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** featured a total of **28 sports** disciplines, showcasing the diverse athletic talent across the country.
 
• The games were hosted by the state of **Bihar** for the first time in the history of the tournament, with the primary venues located in **Patna** and **Rajgir**.
 
• The event took place in **January 2025**, continuing the tradition of holding the games during the school and college winter break to maximize student participation.
 
• The inclusion of **28 sports** reflects the steady expansion of the Khelo India initiative, which aims to provide a platform for young athletes in both Olympic and traditional Indian sports.
 
• More than **6,000 athletes** from all **States and Union Territories** participated in the competition, competing for medals and the chance to be identified for long-term athlete development programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evolution of Khelo India:**
 
 
• The program was originally launched as the **Khelo India School Games** in **2018** in **New Delhi**.
 
• In **2019**, the scope was expanded, and it was renamed the **Khelo India Youth Games**, allowing for two categories: **Under-17** school students and **Under-21** college students.
 
 
 
• **Host States History:**
 
 
• The **2024** edition was held in **Tamil Nadu**, while the **2023** edition was hosted by **Madhya Pradesh** across eight different cities.
 
• **Maharashtra** and **Haryana** have historically been the most successful states, often topping the medal tally in various editions.
 
 
 
• **Inclusion of Indigenous Sports:**
 
 
• One of the unique features of the Khelo India Youth Games is the promotion of traditional Indian sports such as **Gatka**, **Kalaripayattu**, **Thang-Ta**, **Silambam**, and **Mallakhamba**.
 
• These sports are included alongside mainstream disciplines like **Athletics**, **Swimming**, **Archery**, **Wrestling**, and **Boxing**.
 
 
 
• **Scholarship and Support:**
 
 
• The **Talent Identification Development Committee (TIDC)** identifies promising athletes during these games.
 
• Selected athletes receive an annual financial assistance of **Rs. 5 lakh** for **8 years** to support their training and preparation for international events like the **Olympics**.
 
 
 
• **Organizational Structure:**
 
 
• The games are organized by the **Sports Authority of India (SAI)** in collaboration with the **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)** and the respective host state government.
 
• The primary objective of the **Khelo India Program** is to revive the sports culture in India at the grass-root level by building a strong framework for all sports played in the country.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Bihar Government** invested heavily in sports infrastructure for the **2025** games, notably the **State Sports Academy and Bihar Sports University** in **Rajgir**.
 
• The mascot for the games often highlights the local biodiversity or cultural heritage of the host state; for Bihar, the focus remained on its **rich historical legacy** and **environmental symbols**.
 
• The **Khelo India Youth Games** serves as a crucial feeder system for the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)**, ensuring a pipeline of world-class athletes for India.
</ul

questions.question: When was the UNDP Human Development Report 2025, based on 2023 data, released?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 May 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** officially released the **Human Development Report (HDR) 2025** on **6 May 2025**.
 
• This specific report is based on comprehensive global data collected and analyzed for the year **2023**, providing a retrospective look at human progress two years prior to the release.
 
• The **Human Development Report** is an annual milestone publication that assesses the state of human development globally, focusing on metrics beyond mere economic growth.
 
• It introduces the **Human Development Index (HDI)** rankings for member nations, which serves as a critical benchmark for international comparison of social and economic development levels.
 
• The release date of **6 May 2025** was chosen to ensure the inclusion of the most accurate and verified statistical indicators from various international data agencies for the **2023** period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):**
 
 
• The **HDI** is a composite index that measures average achievement in three basic dimensions: a **long and healthy life**, **knowledge**, and a **decent standard of living**.
 
• It was first introduced in **1990** by Pakistani economist **Mahbub ul Haq** and Indian Nobel laureate **Amartya Sen**.
 
• The indicators used include **Life Expectancy at Birth**, **Expected Years of Schooling**, **Mean Years of Schooling**, and **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita**.
 
 
 
• **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP):**
 
 
• The **UNDP** is the UN's global development network, established on **22 November 1965**.
 
• Headquartered in **New York City**, it works in nearly **170 countries** to help eliminate poverty and achieve sustainable economic growth and human development.
 
• The organization publishes the **HDR** to shift the focus of development economics from national income accounting to people-centered policies.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 2025 Report:**
 
 
• By utilizing **2023** data, the **2025** report captures the long-term trends and recovery patterns following global disruptions, such as health crises and geopolitical shifts.
 
• It often includes supplementary indices like the **Gender Inequality Index (GII)** and the **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)** to provide a holistic view of global challenges.
 
• The report serves as a primary resource for **governments**, **NGOs**, and **researchers** to formulate policies that target specific gaps in education, healthcare, and income parity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **HDR 2025** release on **6 May 2025** highlights the importance of data transparency and the lag time required for the **United Nations** to verify **2023** statistics across all sovereign territories.
 
• The report typically categorizes countries into four groups: **Very High**, **High**, **Medium**, and **Low** Human Development, based on their **HDI** score which ranges from **0 to 1**.
 
• Recent reports have increasingly focused on the **Planetary pressures-adjusted Human Development Index (PHDI)**, reflecting the impact of **carbon emissions** and **material footprint** on global progress.
</ul

questions.question: The Fit India Movement's premier cycling event, promoting fitness and pollution solutions, was staged at Mumbai's Gateway of India in February 2025, under what name?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sundays on Cycle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The event titled **Sundays on Cycle** was organized as a premier cycling initiative under the **Fit India Movement** to promote a healthy lifestyle and environmental sustainability.
 
• Staged in **February 2025**, the event commenced from the iconic **Gateway of India** in **Mumbai**, attracting thousands of participants, including fitness enthusiasts, professional cyclists, and celebrities.
 
• The core objective of the **Sundays on Cycle** event is to provide a solution to rising **pollution** levels by encouraging citizens to use **bicycles** for short commutes, thereby reducing the **carbon footprint**.
 
• It serves as a platform to raise awareness about **physical fitness** and the **mental health** benefits associated with regular outdoor activities, aligning with the national vision of a **Pliant and Healthy India**.
 
• The event was supported by various **government ministries** and **local municipal corporations** to ensure a car-free experience on designated routes during the event hours.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fit India Movement:**
 
 
• Launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on **August 29, 2019**, on the occasion of **National Sports Day**.
 
• The movement aims to bring about a behavioral change and move towards a more physically active lifestyle to combat lifestyle diseases like **diabetes**, **obesity**, and **hypertension**.
 
 
 
• **National Sports Day:**
 
 
• Celebrated every year on **August 29** to commemorate the birth anniversary of the Indian hockey legend, **Major Dhyan Chand**.
 
• This day serves as the backdrop for many national health and sports initiatives, including the **National Sports Awards**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Benefits of Cycling:**
 
 
• Cycling is a **zero-emission** mode of transport that helps in reducing **greenhouse gas emissions** and mitigating **urban air pollution**.
 
• Cities like **Mumbai**, **Delhi**, and **Bengaluru** are increasingly adopting **cycle tracks** and **public bike-sharing systems** to promote sustainable urban mobility.
 
 
 
• **Health Advantages:**
 
 
• Regular **cycling** improves **cardiovascular fitness**, increases **muscle strength** and flexibility, and decreases **stress levels**.
 
• It is recognized as one of the most effective aerobic exercises for all **age groups**, contributing significantly to the **Fit India** mission's goals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Sundays on Cycle** initiative is often linked with the "**Cycles4Change**" challenge, which was a part of the **Smart Cities Mission** under the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)**.
 
• During the **February 2025** event, special "**Green Corridors**" were created in **South Mumbai** to ensure the safety of the participants and to demonstrate the feasibility of **dedicated cycling infrastructure** in metropolitan cities.
 
• Such events are crucial for **India's** commitment to the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, specifically **Goal 3 (Good Health and Well-being)** and **Goal 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities)**.
</ul

questions.question: Who received the Sahitya Akademi Translation Prize 2024 (awarded in March 2025) for translating a Malayalam autobiography into Tamil?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P Vimala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **P. Vimala** has been honored with the **Sahitya Akademi Translation Prize 2024** for her exceptional work in translating a **Malayalam** autobiography into **Tamil**.
 
• The translation is based on the **autobiography** of the legendary **Kerala** political leader **K. R. Gowri Amma**, originally titled **Atmakatha**. In **Tamil**, the translated work is titled **K. R. Gowri Amma: Suya Charitham**.
 
• The **Sahitya Akademi** announced the winners for the **2024** translation awards across various Indian languages, and the formal presentation ceremony is scheduled for **March 2025**.
 
• The prize is awarded to the best translation published in the **five years** immediately preceding the year of the award (between **January 2018** and **December 2022** for the 2024 cycle).
 
• This recognition highlights **P. Vimala's** contribution to cross-cultural literature and her skill in bringing the life story of a prominent **Communist leader** and social reformer to the **Tamil**-speaking audience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sahitya Akademi Translation Prize:**
 
 
• Instituted in **1989**, this prize is awarded annually by **India's National Academy of Letters** to encourage translations of high literary quality.
 
• The award carries a **cash prize** of **Rs. 50,000** along with a **citation** and an engraved plaque.
 
• It aims to promote **national integration** by making literature from one Indian language accessible to readers of another language.
 
 
 
• **Other Awardees for 2024:**
 
 
• **Chandan Negi**: She won the **Sahitya Akademi Translation Prize 2024** in the **Punjabi** language category for her translation of **The Legend of Lakshmi Prasad** (originally by **Twinkle Khanna** in **English**).
 
• **Uttara Bwiswmuthiary**: A recipient of the **2024** prize for **Bodo** translation, she translated the **Assamese** novel **Aseema** (written by **Kanchan Baruah**) into the **Bodo** language.
 
• **Madan Soni**: He received the prize in the **Hindi** category for translating the classic **Kannada** novel **Samskara**, written by the Jnanpith awardee **U.R. Ananthamurthy**.
 
 
 
• **K. R. Gowri Amma (Original Author):**
 
 
• She was one of the founding leaders of the **Communist movement** in **Kerala** and the **first woman minister** in independent **Kerala (1957)**.
 
• Her **autobiography** provides deep insights into the **land reforms** and the socio-political evolution of **Kerala** during the **20th century**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Sahitya Akademi**, established on **March 12, 1954**, functions as an autonomous organization under the **Ministry of Culture**, Government of India.
 
• The selection for the **Translation Prize** is made by a **three-member Selection Committee** for each language, following a rigorous process of evaluation.
 
• The award year **2024** saw winners across **24 Indian languages**, including **Sanskrit**, **English**, and major regional languages, reinforcing the linguistic diversity of the nation.
 
• Recipients are selected based on the **accuracy**, **stylistic merit**, and **readability** of the translated text compared to the original work.
</ul

questions.question: During the National Conference on ‘Opportunities of Defence Manufacturing in the Country’ (October 7, 2025), which new portal was launched in India to streamline export and import authorisations in the defence sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Defence Exim Portal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Defence Exim Portal** was officially launched during the National Conference on ‘Opportunities of Defence Manufacturing in the Country’ held on **October 7, 2025**.
 
• This portal is a significant digital initiative by the **Ministry of Defence**, aimed at consolidating and streamlining the processes related to **export and import authorisations** in the Indian defence sector.
 
• The primary objective of the portal is to enhance the **Ease of Doing Business** by providing a **Single Window** interface for Indian defence exporters and importers to interact with regulatory authorities.
 
• It replaces manual or fragmented digital systems with an integrated **end-to-end digital solution**, allowing for **real-time tracking** of applications, which ensures high levels of **transparency** and **accountability** in the administrative workflow.
 
• The portal is designed to significantly reduce the **turnaround time** for obtaining necessary clearances, thereby making the Indian defence industry more competitive in the global market. ***Hence, the correct answer is Defence Exim Portal.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Growth of Defence Exports:**
 
 
• India’s defence exports have reached an unprecedented milestone, crossing **₹21,083 crore** in the financial year **2023-24**, reflecting a growth of over **30%** compared to the previous year.
 
• The government has set an ambitious target to achieve defence exports worth **₹50,000 crore** by the year **2028-29**.
 
 
 
• **Aatmanirbharta in Defence:**
 
 
• The launch of the portal aligns with the vision of **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India), aiming to transform India from a net importer to a significant **global exporter** of defence equipment.
 
• The **Department of Defence Production (DDP)** has been instrumental in notifying **Positive Indigenisation Lists**, which mandate that certain items be procured only from domestic sources.
 
 
 
• **Make in India Initiative:**
 
 
• Under the **Make in India** program, the government has simplified the **Industrial Licensing** process and increased the **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** limit to **74%** through the automatic route in the defence sector.
 
• Strategic partnerships and **Defence Excellence (iDEX)** are fostering innovation among **MSMEs** and **Startups** to create cutting-edge technology for the **Armed Forces**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Department of Defence Production (DDP):** The **DDP** is the nodal agency responsible for the development and regulation of the defence industry and the implementation of the **Defence Exim Portal**.
 
• **Simplification of Procedures:** The portal facilitates the online filing of applications for **Export Authorisations**, **No Objection Certificates (NOCs)**, and **End User Certificates**, which are critical for international trade in sensitive technologies.
 
• **Global Outreach:** By digitizing the EXIM process, India aims to strengthen its ties with friendly foreign nations through the timely supply of high-quality military hardware, including the **BrahMos Missile**, **Tejas Aircraft**, and various **Artillery Systems**.
 
• **Policy Framework:** The **Defence Acquisition Procedure (DAP) 2020** further supports these digital reforms by prioritizing **Buy {Indian-IDDM}** (Indigenously Designed, Developed and Manufactured) categories to boost local production.

questions.question: The International Big Cat Alliance became a treaty-based organisation in January 2025. Under which ministry does it operate?

options.text: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change

questions.solution:
p>The correct answer is __**Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA)** is a global initiative led by **India** that operates under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**.
 
• In **January 2025**, the alliance officially transitioned into a **treaty-based international organization**, following the approval of its framework by the **Union Cabinet** and the subsequent signing of the treaty by several range countries.
 
• The primary goal of the **IBCA** is to ensure the survival and conservation of the **seven big cat species** found globally, namely the **Tiger**, **Lion**, **Leopard**, **Snow Leopard**, **Cheetah**, **Jaguar**, and **Puma**.
 
• The **headquarters** of the **International Big Cat Alliance** is established in **India**, serving as a central hub for coordinating conservation efforts across **96 big cat range countries** and other non-range countries and international organizations.
 
• The **Union Cabinet**, chaired by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, had earlier approved the establishment of the **IBCA** in **February 2024** with a focused one-time budgetary support. ***Hence, the correct answer is the Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Launch Details:**
 
 
• The **International Big Cat Alliance** was formally launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on **April 9, 2023**.
 
• The launch took place in **Mysuru**, **Karnataka**, during a mega event organized to commemorate the **50th anniversary** of **Project Tiger**.
 
 
 
• **Financial Support:**
 
 
• The **Government of India** committed a total financial assistance of **Rs. 150 crore** for a period of **five years**, spanning from **2023-24** to **2027-28**.
 
• This funding is intended to support the initial setup, secretariat operations, and core conservation projects of the alliance.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Strategy:**
 
 
• The alliance focuses on **knowledge sharing**, **capacity building**, and **technical assistance** among member countries to mitigate human-wildlife conflict.
 
• It aims to promote **eco-tourism** and sustainable livelihoods for communities living near big cat habitats, especially in the **Global South**.
 
 
 
• **Member Species:**
 
 
• Out of the seven big cats, **five** species (**Tiger**, **Lion**, **Leopard**, **Snow Leopard**, and **Cheetah**) are naturally found in **India** (Cheetah being recently reintroduced).
 
• The inclusion of **Jaguar** and **Puma** allows for a truly global cooperation including **South American** and **North American** range countries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Organizational Structure:**
 
 
• The **IBCA** consists of a **General Assembly**, which is the supreme decision-making body, a **Council**, and a **Secretariat** based in **India**.
 
• The **Environment Minister** of **India** often represents the nation at the high-level meetings regarding the alliance's treaty framework.
 
 
 
• **Legal and Treaty Status:**
 
 
• The transition to a **treaty-based organization** in **January 2025** provides the **IBCA** with a **legal personality** similar to other international bodies like the **International Solar Alliance (ISA)**.
 
• This status enables the alliance to enter into agreements with other international agencies and receive funding from multilateral development banks.
 
 
 
• **Global Leadership:**
 
 
• By leading the **IBCA**, **India** strengthens its position as a global leader in biodiversity conservation, having successfully increased its own populations of **Tigers** and **Lions**.
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** oversees the implementation of the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**, which provides the domestic legal framework for big cat protection in the country.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following agencies conducted maiden flight-tests of an Integrated Air Defence Weapon System in August 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** successfully conducted the maiden flight-tests of the indigenous **Integrated Air Defence Weapon System** in **August 2025**.
 
• The tests were carried out at the **Integrated Test Range (ITR)** in **Chandipur**, off the coast of **Odisha**, to validate the system's interception capabilities against high-speed aerial threats.
 
• This weapon system is designed to provide a **multi-layered** defense umbrella, capable of neutralizing **Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs)**, fighter aircraft, and incoming cruise missiles.
 
• The flight-test achieved all mission objectives, including the successful tracking of targets by **Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA)** radars and precise engagement by the interceptor missiles.
 
• The successful trial in **August 2025** marks a significant milestone in India's quest for **self-reliance** in critical defense technologies under the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** mission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO):**
 
 
• It was established in **1958** by merging the Technical Development Establishment of the **Indian Army** and the Directorate of Technical Development & Production with the Defence Science Organisation.
 
• Headquartered in **New Delhi**, it operates under the **Ministry of Defence** and aims to empower India with cutting-edge defense technologies.
 
• Major successful programs include the **Agni** and **Prithvi** series of missiles, **Tejas** Light Combat Aircraft, and the **Arjun** Main Battle Tank.
 
 
 
• **Air Defence Systems in India:**
 
 
• India utilizes a variety of systems including the **Akash** missile system, which is a short-range surface-to-air missile (**SAM**) system developed by **DRDO**.
 
• The **MRSAM** (Medium Range Surface-to-Air Missile) is another critical asset developed in collaboration with **Israel** to protect vital installations.
 
• The integration of various sensors and weapon platforms into a single command network is the core objective of the **Integrated Air Defence** strategy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Integrated Air Defence Weapon System** tested in **August 2025** features a high level of **automation**, significantly reducing the reaction time required to counter saturation attacks.
 
• The **Integrated Test Range (ITR)** at **Chandipur** is a world-class facility that provides the necessary infrastructure for the performance evaluation of rockets, missiles, and airborne weapon systems.
 
• With the induction of such systems, the **Indian Armed Forces**—comprising the **Army**, **Navy**, and **Air Force**—gain a unified defensive posture against modern **Electronic Warfare** and stealth technologies.
 
• The participation of private sector industries in the manufacturing of components for this system highlights the growing **Defence Industrial Base** in the **country**.

questions.question: On which date is International Sex Workers' Day observed annually in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 June**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **International Sex Workers' Day** is observed annually on **2 June** to honor sex workers and acknowledge their often-exploitative working conditions.
 
• The origin of this day dates back to **1975**, when more than **100 sex workers** occupied the **Saint-Nizier Church** in **Lyon, France**.
 
• The occupation was a protest against **police brutality**, **fines**, and the **criminalization** of their livelihood, which forced them to work in secret and dangerous environments.
 
• On **10 June 1975**, the police brutally cleared the church, but the movement had already gained international attention, leading to the establishment of the day as a global event.
 
• In **India**, various collectives and **Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs)** observe this day to demand **labor rights**, **social security**, and the **decriminalization** of sex work to ensure the safety of those involved.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance and Symbols:**
 
 
• The **Red Umbrella** is the global symbol for **sex workers' rights**. It was first used by sex workers in **Venice, Italy**, in **2001** during the **49th Venice Biennale**.
 
• The day is also colloquially known as **International Whores' Day** in many parts of the world, reclaiming the term to fight against social stigma.
 
 
 
• **Related Observances:**
 
 
• **International Day to End Violence Against Sex Workers** is observed on **December 17** every year. It focuses on the high rates of **violence** and **hate crimes** committed against the community.
 
• **International Sex Workers' Rights Day** is celebrated on **March 3**, which specifically emphasizes the **human rights** aspect and legal protections.
 
 
 
• **Context in India:**
 
 
• In **India**, sex work is governed by the **Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 (ITPA)**. While the act of selling sex is not per se illegal, activities like **pimping**, **operating a brothel**, and **soliciting** in public are criminalized.
 
• Major organizations like the **Durbar Mahila Samanwaya Committee (DMSC)** in **Kolkata** (Sonagachi) and the **All India Network of Sex Workers (AINSW)** play a vital role in advocating for the community's welfare.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Judicial Interventions:**
 
 
• The **Supreme Court of India**, in the case of **Budhadev Karmaskar v. State of West Bengal (2011)**, stated that sex workers are also entitled to a life of **dignity** under **Article 21** of the **Constitution**.
 
• In **May 2022**, the **Supreme Court** directed that police should neither **interfere** nor **take criminal action** against adult sex workers participating in consensual sex work, recognizing it as a **profession**.
 
 
 
• **Health and Welfare:**
 
 
• The **National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO)** works extensively with sex workers through **Targeted Interventions (TI)** to reduce the prevalence of **HIV/AIDS** and other **STIs**.
 
• The **Government of India** provides various **social welfare schemes**, including the distribution of **Aadhaar cards** and **ration cards** to sex workers following the **Supreme Court's** directions during the **COVID-19 pandemic**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: What is the rank of India in the World Economic Forum’s 2025 Energy Transition Index?

• The index benchmarks countries based on two main pillars: **System Performance** (which includes energy equity, security, and sustainability) and **Transition Readiness** (the enabling environment for future changes).
 
• **India** is recognized for its significant improvements in **energy equity** and **security**, driven by massive **electrification** programs and the expansion of its **renewable energy** portfolio.
 
• The report emphasizes that while India is making strides in **solar** and **wind** energy, maintaining a balance between economic growth and **environmental sustainability** remains a critical challenge.

• The **WEF** is an **international non-governmental organization** established on **24 January 1971**.
 
• It is headquartered in **Cologny, Switzerland**, and is best known for its annual meeting in **Davos**.
 
• The organization promotes public-private cooperation to shape global, regional, and industry agendas.
 
 
 
• **Global Rankings:**
 
 
• Nordic countries consistently lead the **Energy Transition Index**. For recent cycles, **Sweden** has often occupied the **1st rank**, followed by **Denmark** and **Finland**.
 
• These countries are praised for their advanced **carbon pricing** mechanisms and high share of **non-fossil fuel** energy in their total mix.
 
 
 
• **India's Energy Targets:**

• **The Energy Triangle:** The **ETI** framework evaluates the "Energy Triangle," which consists of **Economic Development and Growth**, **Environmental Sustainability**, and **Energy Access and Security**.
 
• **Transition Readiness:** This evaluates the robustness of a country's **institutional framework**, **capital and investment**, **innovation**, and **human capital** dedicated to energy transition.
 
• **Global Trends:** The **2025** report notes a slowdown in the global pace of energy transition due to geopolitical tensions and **energy security** concerns, making **India**'s progress particularly noteworthy.
 
• **Data Source:** The **World Economic Forum** collaborates with **Accenture** to produce this comprehensive analysis, involving data from the **International Energy Agency (IEA)** and other global energy bodies.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following Indian states conducted a large-scale disaster drill in November 2025, focusing on oil and chemical disaster preparedness at major industrial hubs?

__
 
• The state of **Gujarat** successfully executed a state-wide large-scale disaster management drill in **November 2025**, specifically designed to test the readiness of industrial sectors against hazardous incidents.

• The drill was concentrated in major industrial corridors and hubs such as **Jamnagar**, **Dahej**, **Mundra**, and **Hazira**, which house some of the largest refineries and chemical complexes in the **world**.
 
• Participating agencies included the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)**, the **State Disaster Response Force (SDRF)**, the **Indian Coast Guard**, and various **District Disaster Management Authorities (DDMAs)**.
 
• The primary objective was to validate the **Chemical (Industrial) Disaster Management Plan** and ensure effective coordination between **Government** bodies and **private sector** stakeholders during a simulated emergency. ***Hence, the correct answer is Gujarat.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• The state is often referred to as the **Petro-capital of India**, contributing significantly to the national output of **petroleum products** and **chemicals**.
 
• **Jamnagar** hosts the world's largest oil refinery complex, while **Dahej** is home to one of India's few **Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemicals Investment Regions (PCPIR)**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Framework:**
 
 
• Industrial safety in India is regulated under the **Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemical (MSIHC) Rules, 1989**, which mandates regular safety audits and mock drills.
 
• The **Gujarat State Disaster Management Authority (GSDMA)**, established under the **Gujarat State Disaster Management Act, 2003**, is the nodal agency for planning and implementing disaster mitigation strategies in the state.
 
 
 
• **Types of Emergency Plans:**
 
 
• **On-site Emergency Plan:** This is prepared by the **occupier** of the industrial facility to deal with emergencies within the factory premises.

• **NDRF and SDRF:** The **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** was constituted under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**. It plays a critical role in specialized response to **Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN)** disasters.
 
• **Technological Integration:** During the **2025** drill, advanced tools like **drones** for aerial surveillance, **GIS mapping** for hazard zones, and **real-time communication** systems were utilized to enhance response speed.
 
• **Maritime Safety:** Since **Gujarat** has the longest coastline in **India** (approx **1600 km**), the drill also included simulations for **oil spills** at major ports like **Kandla (Deendayal Port)** and **Mundra** to protect marine **ecosystems**.

questions.question: According to the PIB release 'Proactive Measures taken by CAQM to contain Air Pollution' (10 November 2025), farm fire incidents in Haryana between 15 September and 9 November 2025 fell by roughly what percentage compared to the same period in 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**About 65%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Press Information Bureau (PIB)** release titled 'Proactive Measures taken by CAQM to contain Air Pollution' dated **10 November 2025**, there has been a significant decline in farm fire incidents in the northern states.
 
• For the state of **Haryana**, the total number of farm fire incidents recorded between **15 September and 9 November 2025** showed a remarkable reduction of **About 65%** compared to the same period in **2024**.
 
• This data is monitored and reported by the **Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM)** using a **Standard Protocol** developed by **ISRO** to track **Active Fire Events (AFE)**.
 
• The reduction is attributed to the strict implementation of the **State Action Plan**, which involves both **In-situ** and **Ex-situ** crop residue management strategies.
 
• The decline in incidents in **Haryana** is a crucial factor in managing the **Air Quality Index (AQI)** of the **National Capital Region (NCR)**, which typically deteriorates during the onset of winter due to stubble burning.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is About 65%.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM)**:
 
 
• The **CAQM** is a **statutory body** formed under the **Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas Act, 2021**.
 
• It was established to ensure better coordination, research, identification, and resolution of problems surrounding the **air quality index** in the **NCR** and adjoining areas like **Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh**.
 
 
 
• **Stubble Burning (Parali)**:
 
 
• This practice involves setting fire to the straw stubble that remains after harvesting grains like **Paddy**.
 
• It is primarily done to quickly clear the fields for the **Rabi** crop (wheat) sowing season.
 
• Burning releases large amounts of **Carbon Monoxide (CO)**, **Methane (CH4)**, and **Particulate Matter (PM2.5 and PM10)** into the atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP)**:
 
 
• **GRAP** is an emergency framework implemented by the **CAQM** to prevent further deterioration of air quality.
 
• It is divided into four stages: **Stage I - 'Poor'** (AQI 201-300), **Stage II - 'Very Poor'** (AQI 301-400), **Stage III - 'Severe'** (AQI 401-450), and **Stage IV - 'Severe Plus'** (AQI > 450).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Crop Residue Management (CRM) Scheme**:
 
 
• The **Central Government** provides funds under the **CRM scheme** to subsidize machinery like **Super Seeders**, **Happy Seeders**, and **Bio-decomposers**.
 
• Farmers receive a **50% subsidy** for individual machinery and **80% subsidy** for establishing **Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs)**.
 
 
 
• **Legal and Monitoring Actions**:
 
 
• The **Supreme Court of India** has frequently intervened to direct states to provide incentives to farmers to avoid burning.
 
• **Environmental Compensation (EC)** is imposed on farmers found violating the ban on stubble burning, with rates fixed based on the **acreage of the land**.
 
• In **2025**, the use of **remote sensing technology** and **flying squads** helped in real-time detection and prevention of fire incidents in **Haryana** and **Punjab**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which summit in July 2025 emphasised Global South cooperation under Brazil’s chairmanship?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**BRICS Summit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brazil** officially assumed the **chairmanship** of the **BRICS** group for the year **2025**, succeeding **Russia**.
 
• The **BRICS Summit** held in **July 2025** placed a significant emphasis on **Global South cooperation**, reflecting **Brazil's** long-standing foreign policy priority of fostering ties among developing nations.
 
• Under **Brazil’s** leadership, the summit focused on critical issues such as **inequality reduction**, **combating hunger**, and the **reform of international financial institutions** like the **IMF** and **World Bank** to better represent emerging economies.
 
• The **2025 Summit** served as a platform for the recently expanded **BRICS+** members to align their strategies on **climate action** and **sustainable development** ahead of **COP30**, which **Brazil** is also scheduled to host.
 
• The emphasis on the **Global South** was intended to strengthen the collective bargaining power of nations in **Africa**, **Asia**, and **Latin America** within the global geopolitical landscape. ***Hence, the correct answer is the BRICS Summit.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **BRICS Expansion:** Originally composed of **Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa**, the group expanded in **January 2024** to include **Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates**, enhancing its representation of the **Global South**.
 
• **Global South:** This term refers to various countries often characterized as "developing" or "newly industrialized," primarily located in the **Southern Hemisphere**. It represents a shift in global economic power toward **non-Western** nations.
 
• **G7 Summit:** The **Group of Seven** consists of advanced economies including the **USA, UK, France, Germany, Italy, Canada, and Japan**. Unlike **BRICS**, it represents the **Global North** and traditional economic powers.
 
• **APEC Summit:** The **Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation** is a regional economic forum established in **1989** to leverage the growing interdependence of the **Asia-Pacific**. It includes **21 member economies** but is not focused exclusively on the **Global South**.
 
• **ASEAN Summit:** The **Association of Southeast Asian Nations** is a regional organization that promotes economic, political, and security cooperation among its **10 member states** in **Southeast Asia**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **New Development Bank (NDB):** Often called the **BRICS Bank**, this institution is headquartered in **Shanghai** and provides financing for infrastructure projects in **BRICS** and other emerging economies, acting as an alternative to the **World Bank**.
 
• **Rotating Chairmanship:** The **BRICS chairmanship** rotates annually among its members. During its **2025** tenure, **Brazil** pushed for the use of **local currencies** in international trade to reduce dependence on the **US Dollar**.
 
• **Geopolitical Influence:** Collectively, **BRICS** members represent over **40% of the world's population** and a significant portion of global **GDP**, making their summits crucial for global economic governance.
 
• **Strategic Themes:** Brazil's **2025** agenda also included **energy transition** and **digital transformation**, aiming to bridge the digital divide between the **Global North** and **Global South**.

questions.question: As per the World Bank's Spring 2025 report, how many people did India lift out of extreme poverty over the past decade?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**171 million**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• According to the **World Bank's Spring 2025** report titled **"South Asia Development Update"**, India has made significant strides in poverty reduction, lifting approximately **171 million** people out of extreme poverty over the past decade. 
 
• The assessment is based on the **International Poverty Line** of **$2.15 per person per day** (measured at **2017 Purchasing Power Parity** prices). 
 
• The data indicates that the headcount poverty ratio in India declined from **21.6%** in **2011-12** to around **8%** to **10%** by the end of the decade ending in **2021-22**. 
 
• This massive reduction highlights the impact of sustained **Economic Growth** and the expansion of **Social Welfare Programs** across the country. 
 
• The report notes that India's performance was a major driver for the overall poverty reduction statistics in the **South Asian region**, despite the economic disruptions caused by the **COVID-19 pandemic**. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Extreme Poverty Definition:** The **World Bank** updated the global poverty line in **September 2022** from **$1.90** to **$2.15** to reflect changes in **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** and the cost of living globally. 
 
• **Role of HCES:** The **Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) 2022-23**, released by the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**, provided the necessary data for economists to calculate recent poverty trends in **India**. 
 
• **Government Interventions:** Key schemes such as the **Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY)**, which provided free foodgrains to over **80 crore** people, and the **Jal Jeevan Mission**, have been credited with improving the quality of life and reducing vulnerability. 
 
• **Multidimensional Poverty:** Apart from income-based measures, the **NITI Aayog’s Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)** also showed a sharp decline, with **24.82 crore** people escaping multidimensional poverty over the last **9 years**. 
 
• **Global Context:** India's achievement is considered one of the largest migrations out of poverty in **human history**, comparable to the poverty reduction seen in **China** during previous decades. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Timeline:** The "past decade" referenced in the **Spring 2025** report primarily covers the period from **2011-12** to **2021-22**, using the most recent **World Bank** modeling. 
 
• **Economic Resilience:** Despite global headwinds, the report emphasizes that India remains the **fastest-growing major economy**, which is a prerequisite for generating the resources needed for **poverty alleviation**. 
 
• **Data Reliability:** The **World Bank** utilizes various sources, including **official government surveys** and **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** data, to ensure the **171 million** figure accurately represents the shift in **disposable income** levels.

__
 
• **National Awards for e-Governance:**

• The awards aim to recognize and promote excellence in the implementation of **e-Governance** initiatives and to encourage the use of **Information and Communication Technology (ICT)** in government processes.
 
• There are usually multiple categories, including excellence in government process re-engineering, digital transformation, and research on citizen-centric services.

• Current initiatives like **UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik)** and **Digi Yatra** are part of the ministry's vision to make flying accessible and high-tech for all.

• **Data Privacy and Security:**
 
 
• One of the most critical features of **Digi Yatra** is its **decentralized storage** system. The **Personally Identifiable Information (PII)** of the passenger is stored locally on the user's mobile device in a **distributed ledger**.
 
• The data is not stored in any central server; it is shared with the airport of departure only for the duration of the flight and is purged within **24 hours** of the flight's departure.
 
 
 
• **Implementation Status:**
 
 
• Initially launched at airports in **Delhi, Bengaluru, and Varanasi** in **December 2022**, the service has since expanded to major cities like **Hyderabad, Pune, Vijayawada, and Kolkata**.
 
• By **2024-2025**, the government aims to implement **Digi Yatra** across all major airports in the country to standardize the digital travel experience.
 
 
 
• **Technology Stack:**
 
 
• It utilizes **W3C standards** for **Verifiable Credentials** and **Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs)**, ensuring that India's digital public infrastructure remains at the forefront of global technological standards.
